approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecule by drawing atom, bond, path and ring edits, normalizing their molecular identities, and directly evaluating the first full batch allowed by inverse-motif memory. Both inverse signs from the same selected transition must match to veto a fresh neighbor. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph even when its score is worse, and a separate archive retains the best score. The current deletion choices remove one leaf atom or contract one degree-two atom, so removal of a longer pendant substituent requires several separately evaluated transitions. Identity normalization, memory lifetime and accepted-score selection are already established parts of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Extend the existing deletion menu with a whole pendant-branch choice. When the deletion operator is drawn, it may remove an entire acyclic substituent attached through one single bond to a ring atom, while retaining every ring atom and the connections among retained atoms. Single-leaf choices remain in the same menu, and the operator keeps its existing allocation weight. This adds direct compact neighbors that no existing one-step removal can reach. The earlier sulfur sibling filtered local valence; this experiment changes the size of a permitted deletion and does not inherit or add that filter.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 has a complete macro mean of 0.5209178281192797 and standard deviation 0.004890242222897396. Its saved fifteen task logs contain 4350 emitted neighbors: 1504 increase atom count and 716 decrease it. The existing delete_leaf and contract_atom operations remove only one atom at a time; 394 emitted neighbors are single-leaf deletions. Its molecular assessment describes bulky decorated late families whose peripheral changes can have identical scores. An offline topological examination of its actual batch-start source graphs finds an eligible multi-atom pendant acyclic branch in 399 of 435 states and at 453 of 489 actual delete_leaf draws. Summed across those batch-start states, 740 topological branch options produce 724 graph-valid products, of which 712 are not in the then-existing proposed-identity set. These are repeated-state opportunity counts and unscored products, not new evaluations or distinct molecules. The new sibling n-93cd9a000278 confirms that restricting sulfur valence changes chemistry, but retains bulky decoration, complex rings and uneven paired scores. It supplies no branch-pruning test. The hypothesized bottleneck is that the current one-atom deletion neighborhood cannot directly offer a compact analogue obtained by removing a whole acyclic substituent while retaining the ring framework.
hypothesis: Extend the Parent's existing uniformly sampled leaf-deletion menu with whole multi-atom acyclic branches attached by one non-ring single bond directly to a ring atom, so the same deletion-operator allocation can emit a compact neighbor in one edit while retaining the complete ring framework.

finding_summary.headline: Whole-branch deletion produced compact neighbors, but every score replica regressed.
finding_summary.insights:
A lack of eligible branches was not the bottleneck: the Parent already had branch opportunities in 399 of 435 states, and the extension successfully turned such opportunities into new evaluated neighbors. The added prunings usually lost source score, rarely won their batch and were followed by regrowth whenever selected. Those observations help explain why immediate reductions of several atoms did not produce a lasting shift toward smaller sampled molecules under the unchanged accepted-score walk.

The experiment separates direct access to compact analogues from retaining useful score. Its complete method loses score in every seed, although that loss cannot be assigned solely to the pruned candidates because the changed menu also changes later sampling and trajectories. The molecular assessment remains dominated by sulfur-rich polycycles, reactive heteroatom bonds and unresolved ring geometry and stereochemistry. Ring-preserving removal alone does not resolve those chemical limitations.
finding_summary.results:
The expanded menu was available in 391 of 435 actual batch-start states. It selected 83 whole-branch edits, all graph-valid; after seven duplicate exclusions and seven tabu vetoes, 69 prunings reached evaluation. Each removed 2-14 heavy atoms in one step, averaging 3.75 atoms and 2.10 rotatable bonds, while retaining every ring atom and bond. The recorded menus, uniform selection, graph edits and identity joins passed the audit, including exact original behavior in all 55 deletion draws where no added branch was available.

Eight of the 69 evaluated prunings beat their source, and four became the next current state. All four later grew again. Typical emitted size remained essentially unchanged at 33.21 heavy atoms, compared with 33.20 for Parent. All three seeds completed their five 300-evaluation tasks; sampling cost was also similar at 12.14 versus 12.15 attempts per ten-member batch.

Mean macro final Top-1 fell from 0.520918 to 0.456635, a paired mean change of -0.064283. The three seed changes were -0.020009, -0.101316 and -0.071524. Every task mean declined, with the largest losses in DRD2 and sitagliptin. The intended neighborhood expansion and immediate size reduction occurred, while the score-retention hypothesis failed on the supplied panel.

molecular.headline: Sulfur-rich polycycles and reactive heteroatom bonds persist despite some recognizable aromatic amide families
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete corresponding Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 trajectories. Ring-closure and branch presence are 1.0 throughout. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.7322 to 1.0, while charge and stereocentre token presence remain 0.0. These counters indicate SMILES features, not aromatic atom fractions, measured basicity or feasible stereochemistry. The output remains chemically close in broad character to the Parent: compact fused aromatic carbonyl compounds, large decorated nitrogen heterocycles, halogenated aromatic amine assemblies, bridged oxygen/nitrogen carbonyl systems and sulfur-rich cages. Several seeds change detailed scaffolds, giving moderate diversity across the panel, but each late trajectory mainly varies a related family. The more conventional indole or aza-indole amides coexist with multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur, sulfur-carbon triple bonds, N-Cl/N-F/O-F bonds, peroxides and extensive constrained ring closure. Overall synthetic plausibility remains poor and drug-like quality weak; recognizable fragments do not make these complete structures accessible. Score changes differ across seeds and do not consistently accompany a move toward more conventional chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-1 family contains moderately sized fused aza-aromatic amides or thioesters, with ethyl/methyl groups, hydroxymethylthio or bromomethylthio substituents and N-Cl on the fused pyrrolic nitrogen. More conventional indole carboxamide and thioester relatives also score well. Other seeds move into bridged thione/amine systems or unsaturated sulfur-rich frameworks. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9678 and halogen presence is 0.8678. Compared with the Parent's indole, benzofuran N-chloroamide and aryl-ketone families, the current high region preserves compact fused aromatic/carbonyl arrangements while changing ring nitrogen and sulfur linkages. Whole-molecule plausibility is compromised by N-Cl, O-F, N-O and unusual sulfur chemistry.
liabilities: N-Cl, O-F, bromomethylthio and thioester groups create reactivity or stability concerns in otherwise recognizable aromatic scaffolds.
Late multiply bonded sulfur and dense bridged thione/amine structures have unresolved geometry and synthetic accessibility.
missing_features: Stable amide and thioester alternatives preserving the favorable fused aromatic arrangement are underrepresented relative to N-halogen, O-halogen and N-O substitutions.
Accessible alternatives to the late bridged or sulfur-rich ring systems and explicit configurations where stereocentres arise are absent from the shown high/final series.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best N-chloro aza-aromatic fluoroanilide scores 0.42749549733373915 versus the Parent seed-1 maximum of 0.39905049777278273. Its nonfluorinated anilide relative scores 0.4103264278932849. An indole thioester and corresponding amide score 0.404945686740228 and 0.39004142494831223, respectively, showing a favorable region without N-Cl on that indole. In contrast, disrupting the carbonyl into a hydroxyalkyl thioether gives 0.04016039186228654, and an expanded partially saturated ring system scores 0.016326676663027142. Compact aromatic/carbonyl placement appears favorable, while reactive N-Cl is not demonstrated to be universally necessary. The other current seeds do not improve over their paired Parent maxima.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest seed-2 molecules are very large substituted fused nitrogen diones linked to sulfur/nitrogen-rich heterocycles. They carry a long brominated polyene or imine-containing side chain, an alkyl-S-O-CH2 substituent, propyl and fluoroalkyl groups. Other seeds generate related diones with polyamines and N-Cl, or expanded nitrogen heterocycles with thioesters, imines and cyclic alkynes. Aromatic-token presence is 1.0 and mean SMILES length is 73.5, consistent with visibly extensive substitution but not itself a size descriptor. This resembles the Parent's heavily decorated heterocyclic chemistry; the latest structures remain difficult complete synthetic targets with labile heteroatom combinations and extensive flexibility.
liabilities: Long halo-polyene chains, imines, thioesters and S-O/N-S combinations add flexibility, reactivity and chemical-compatibility concerns.
Expanded or highly constrained heterocycles and unspecified fluoroalkyl stereochemistry reduce confidence in accessible molecular shape.
missing_features: Compact stable versions of the favorable heterocyclic arrangement are poorly represented among the late, extensively decorated molecules.
Conventional replacements for the alkyl-S-O linkage, reactive imine/haloalkene combinations and unusual heteroaromatic ring arrangements remain underexplored.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best seed-2 molecule scores 0.5966573573049399, below the paired Parent maximum of 0.6092182584436399; the other paired current maxima are also lower. Early altered imino/carbonyl or sulfur-ring examples score 0.526081691583997 and 0.528153827722535. A substantially smaller related heterocycle without the long halo-polyene side chain still scores 0.5940462840248751, so extensive growth is not shown to be necessary. Multiple alkyl and fluoroalkyl variants tie at 0.5926433232056583. Disrupting the peripheral aromatic heterocycle into the final expanded N/S ring lowers the score to 0.5373314793543317. Retained heterocyclic arrangement appears more consistently important than the precise long substituents.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leaders combine halogenated aromatic rings, methoxy or methylthio substitution, an aminomethyl-substituted aziridine, and a small nitrogen/sulfur ring containing a sulfur-carbon triple bond. Additional sulfur centres carry sulfur-sulfur or sulfur-carbon double bonds with further substituents. Every proposal contains aromatic, halogen and ring-closure tokens. Seeds 1 and 2 instead reach other bulky aromatic amine/sulfur assemblies, including dense bridged N/S cages. Relative to the Parent's already unusual sulfur/amine frameworks, the high seed-0 chemistry preserves the aromatic/basic-amine pattern but intensifies sulfur-valence and ring-strain concerns. These are highly implausible complete synthetic targets, despite recognizable aryl and amine fragments.
liabilities: A sulfur-carbon triple bond in a small ring, multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonding raise severe stability and geometry concerns.
Aziridine strain, unspecified substituted-ring stereochemistry and bulky halogenated aromatic surfaces further limit drug-like plausibility.
missing_features: Stable, conventionally bonded realizations of the favorable aromatic/basic-amine spacing are missing from the displayed high-scoring family.
Less strained saturated-ring alternatives with explicit configurations are underrepresented; neutral SMILES alone do not establish relevant amine protonation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The sulfur-triple-bond/aziridine family reaches 0.9296093497966158 versus the Parent seed-0 maximum of 0.8856242185485628. Methoxy versus methylthio and fluoromethyl versus chloromethyl versions share 0.9296093497966158. Increasing the aziridine ring size yields a related molecule at 0.9063259998534903. Early acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives remain low, including 0.007468397818197266. The observations support a later aromatic/amine arrangement but do not establish that the extraordinary sulfur bonding is chemically useful. Current seeds 1 and 2 reach lower maxima than their paired Parent trajectories and end in different sulfur-rich families.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 gives moderately large, heavily bridged carbonyl compounds with aza-aromatic and ethoxyphenyl rings, a cyclic carbamate or lactam, hydroxyl-bearing junctions and an oxygen-rich macrocyclic bridge. These are more recognizable than the sulfur-rich final seed-2 cages, which contain N-O, N-N and unusual hydroxylated hydrogen-bearing sulfur. Seed 1 also explores cyclic cumulated unsaturation and peroxide-containing relatives. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9586, ring-closure presence is 1.0 and cumulated-double-bond presence is 0.1471. Compared with the Parent bridged N-O/carbonyl families, ring and heteroatom elaboration persists rather than yielding clearly simpler chemistry.
liabilities: Macrocyclic closure, hydroxyl-bearing ring junctions and constrained unsaturation leave strain and stereochemical feasibility unresolved.
Peroxide motifs and dense N/O/S networks add potential instability without consistently favorable scores.
missing_features: Accessible simpler ring systems preserving the aromatic/carbamate arrangement are underexplored relative to elaborate macrocyclic and bridged alternatives.
Stable replacements for peroxide, N-O/N-N and unusual sulfur linkages, together with defined ring-junction configurations, are absent from much of the late output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best bridged aza-aromatic carbamate scores 0.20739224495838143, close to but below the Parent seed-0 maximum of 0.2107445781802027. A less extensively bridged aryl cyclic-carbamate relative already scores 0.2038246232140464. Ring-opened or polyene/peroxide variants score 0.12532962632028227 and 0.1317529051523964. Retaining aromatic surfaces with a constrained carbonyl-containing arrangement appears favorable. The final N/O/S-rich bridged family remains near 0.17, including 0.17660664388632322, and shows no clear benefit from the additional heteroatom complexity. The score range does not isolate a unique missing target fragment.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecules are compact nonaromatic sulfur-rich cages with ketone or lactone, aldehyde, N-fluoroamidine/cyclic urea-like functionality and multiple constrained sulfur-carbon bonds. Related high products include sulfur imine functionality, thiols and small unsaturated sulfur rings. Seeds 0 and 1 also contain densely fused sulfur/carbonyl cages, sometimes partly aromatic. Aromatic-token presence is 0.7322 over the whole panel, but the displayed leaders themselves lack aromatic atoms in their SMILES graphs. Compared with the Parent, detailed ring connections and halogen placement change while unusual sulfur valence, reactive N-F and unspecified stereochemistry remain prominent. The complete structures have very poor apparent synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: Multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur, constrained small sulfur rings and dense cage junctions create severe chemical and geometric concerns.
N-F, aldehyde and reactive sulfur functionality coexist without stereochemical specification or evidence of whole-molecule synthetic accessibility.
missing_features: Stable conventional frameworks retaining the favorable carbonyl/nitrogen arrangement without multiply bonded sulfur cages are not demonstrated among the leaders.
Chemically less reactive alternatives to the N-F/aldehyde combination and explicit configurations at cage junctions are absent from the shown comparisons.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best seed-2 cage scores 0.4547680704346094 versus 0.4484554129767839 for its paired Parent; current seeds 0 and 1 have lower maxima than their Parents. The low sulfur/carbonyl cage at 4.906706964908493e-09 shows that sulfur-rich complexity alone is insufficient. In the final family, a related lactone-containing cage scores 0.06842623585263305, whereas the ketone/sulfide arrangement reaches the maximum. Changing the N-fluoroamidine connection gives 0.10586430855837528 or 0.1578665537398357. Local carbonyl, nitrogen and ring connectivity therefore matters strongly, but the evidence does not show a stable accessible realization of that favorable arrangement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes a sulfur-carbon triple bond in a small ring, multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds. Methoxy/methylthio and fluoromethyl/chloromethyl variants of the same sulfur-rich family tie at 0.9296093497966158, while sulfur-rich cage complexity also occurs at very low scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still produces high-scoring molecular arrangements through highly unconventional sulfur bonding.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide ordinary carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and sulfur linkages that preserve existing attachment geometry, and distinguish chemical feasibility from scalar-score agreement. Stable counterparts of the favorable aromatic/amine and carbonyl arrangements are a general generator capability still missing from these leaders.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High or final digest molecules contain N-Cl, N-F, O-F, peroxide, alkyl-S-O and dense N-O/N-N networks. An indole thioester at 0.404945686740228 and its amide counterpart at 0.39004142494831223 show that more conventional carbonyl linkages can already reach part of the favorable region.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reactive nitrogen, oxygen and sulfur linkages remain entangled with otherwise recognizable aromatic carbonyl chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand stable matched alternatives around recurring carbonyl and heteroaromatic attachment patterns, while representing reactive-bond and functional-group compatibility independently. Avoid equating familiar individual fragments with a stable complete molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring-closure presence is 1.0 and stereocentre-token presence is 0.0 in every digest. The leaders include substituted aziridines, hydroxyl-bearing macrocyclic junctions and dense sulfur cages, while cumulated-double-bond presence reaches 0.1471 in one proposal set.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits abundant ring closures without resolving three-dimensional feasibility or stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make accessible ring sizes and less constrained fused or spiro alternatives available, with consistent configuration assignment and stereoisomer variation where applicable. Score sensitivity to those configurations cannot be inferred from the present unspecified structures.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A decorated heterocycle reaches 0.5966573573049399 while a substantially smaller related molecule reaches 0.5940462840248751. A bridged aromatic carbamate at 0.20739224495838143 has a less elaborated relative at 0.2038246232140464. Multiple alkyl/fluoroalkyl variants share 0.5926433232056583.
transferable_gaps.gap: Large side chains and increasingly elaborate ring systems are sampled more extensively than chemically simpler alternatives with comparable observed scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate compact substituents, fewer ring connections and simpler linkers around the existing favorable arrangements. This would expose stable accessible chemistry within score-tolerant regions rather than concentrating late proposals on additional molecular complexity.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
